caption.text: No 90-day miracle. Just one honest year. Save this for the days you feel like quitting 📌 Which month are you on? 👇 #gymmotivation #fitnessjourney #gymbeginner #consistency
caption.notes: Save prompt + question ('which month are you on?') invites comments from people at every stage. No 'lifters'.

text.string: Real progress is slower than the internet shows.
Most early strength comes from your body learning the moves. The mirror barely changes. That's normal.
Other people might not notice yet. You will.
Visible muscle, better posture, and weights that would have scared you on day one.
You Look Like Someone Who Trains
Not a fitness model. But clearly not the person who started a year ago.
3 workouts a week = 156 workouts a year.
Miss a month, lose a month. Showing up is the whole trick.

claims_to_verify: 'Most early strength comes from your body learning the moves': early strength gains are largely neural (well established, e.g. Moritani & deVries, 1979). Verify the citation before quoting it.
Months 3 / 6 / 12 descriptions are deliberately qualitative: no kg or % numbers, because muscle-gain rates vary widely between people.
'3 workouts a week = 156 workouts a year': arithmetic (3 x 52).
Figures must look natural and realistic at every stage — no bodybuilder at Year 1.
